item.title: Chinese premier says ready to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation with Tajikistan
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
DUSHANBE, Oct. 18 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Sunday that China stands ready to work with Tajikistan to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. He made the remarks in talks with Tajik Prime Minister Kokhir Rasulzoda during his official visit, saying China is willing to deeply align its development strategies with Tajikistan, deepen cooperation in trade and investment, green minerals, connectivity, clean energy, artificial intelligence and other areas, so as to better achieve mutual benefit and win-win results. China will import more high-quality goods from Tajikistan, encourage Chinese enterprises to invest and start businesses in Tajikistan, and hopes that Tajikistan will continue to provide a favorable business environment for enterprises, Li added. Both sides should expand exchanges and cooperation in areas such as culture, education, health, sports and local-level fields to enhance the sense of gain of the people of both countries, said Li, noting that at the same time, the two countries should continue to deepen law enforcement and security cooperation to foster a stable and secure environment for personnel exchanges between the two sides. Noting that the international situation continues to undergo complex changes, Li said that as important members of the Global South, China and Tajikistan should unite and coordinate more closely, safeguard the common interests of both countries and defend international fairness and justice. He said the two sides should further strengthen communication and coordination within multilateral frameworks including the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, the China-Central Asia mechanism and the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, and work to build a more just and equitable global governance system. People of China and Tajikistan have always shared friendly sentiments toward each other, Li said, noting that in recent years under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Emomali Rahmon, China-Tajikistan relations have maintained a high level of development, with cooperation across various fields deepening and yielding tangible results. Next year marks the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Tajikistan, Li said, adding that China stands ready to work with Tajikistan to deepen strategic mutual trust, firmly support each other, take all-round cooperation to new heights, deliver more tangible outcomes and better benefit people of both countries. For his part, Rasulzoda said that under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, Tajikistan-China relations are currently at their best level in history. In May this year, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon paid a successful visit to China, and relations between the two countries have entered a new stage of development, Rasulzoda said. China is the most important trade and investment partner of Tajikistan, Rasulzoda said, expressing appreciation for China's long-standing and strong support for Tajikistan's economic development. He said Tajikistan is committed to advancing all-round cooperation with China and stands ready to further leverage such platforms as the China-Tajikistan intergovernmental committee on economic and trade cooperation, promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, and deepen mutually beneficial cooperation in trade, investment, agriculture, transport and logistics, energy and minerals, and connectivity. Rasulzoda also called for expanding cooperation in emerging fields such as the green economy, digital economy and artificial intelligence, enhancing people-to-people exchanges, and strengthening communication and coordination within multilateral frameworks, including the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and the China-Central Asia mechanism, to promote further progress in Tajikistan-China relations. Following the talks, the two sides witnessed the signing of multiple documents covering infrastructure development, education, anti-corruption and standardized cooperation. On Sunday afternoon, Li also laid a wreath at the monument of Ismoil Somoni.

item.title: Chinese premier says Beijing ready to ensure high-quality China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
TASHKENT, Oct. 17 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Saturday that China stands ready to ensure the high-quality implementation of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project. During his meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev here, Li also said that China supports more capable Chinese enterprises in investing and doing business in Uzbekistan and hopes that the Uzbek side will continue to provide a favorable business environment for these enterprises. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Mirziyoyev, the building of a China-Uzbekistan community with a shared future has continued to achieve new results, Li said. In the face of a complex and turbulent international landscape, China and Uzbekistan should strengthen solidarity and cooperation and remain firmly committed to moving forward together, he said. China stands ready to strengthen strategic communication with Uzbekistan, continue to firmly support each other's core interests, and expand mutually beneficial cooperation to deliver greater benefits to the peoples of both countries, Li said. China is ready to work with Uzbekistan to expand bilateral trade and optimize its structure, strengthen cooperation in areas such as energy, minerals, finance, and connectivity, and deepen cooperation in scientific and technological innovation in fields such as artificial intelligence, the green economy, and aerospace, so as to jointly seize future development opportunities, Li said. Both sides should also promote people-to-people connectivity and facilitate the establishment of cultural centers in each other's countries as soon as possible, Li said. China is ready to strengthen coordination of positions with Uzbekistan on major issues, enhance collaboration within multilateral frameworks such as the China-Central Asia mechanism and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), safeguard the common interests of both countries, and contribute to peace and development at both the regional and global levels, Li said. For his part, Mirziyoyev congratulated the Communist Party of China on the 105th anniversary of its founding, saying that under the wise leadership of President Xi, China is forging ahead toward national rejuvenation. Uzbekistan-China relations are currently enjoying a "golden age," he said, adding that his successful meeting with Xi on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek charted the course for advancing bilateral cooperation. Uzbekistan firmly adheres to the one-China principle and firmly supports China in safeguarding its core interests, he said, noting that Uzbekistan will continue to work with China to combat the "three evil forces" of terrorism, separatism and extremism. Uzbekistan welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in the country and stands ready to work with China to accelerate the construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway and advance exchanges and cooperation across various fields, he said. Uzbekistan supports the four global initiatives proposed by Xi and is willing to strengthen communication and coordination with China in multilateral affairs, promoting continued progress in the Uzbekistan-China all-weather comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, he added.

item.title: Chinese premier arrives in Tajikistan for official visit, SCO meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
DUSHANBE, Oct. 18 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang arrived in Dushanbe on Sunday for an official visit to Tajikistan and to attend the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) at the invitation of Tajik Prime Minister Kokhir Rasulzoda. China and Tajikistan are good neighbors, good friends, and good partners, Li said, noting that bilateral relations have developed rapidly in recent years, with fruitful cooperation across various fields that brings tangible benefits to the people of both countries. In May this year, the two heads of state held a meeting in Beijing and drew up a blueprint for deepening China-Tajikistan relations, Li noted. China is ready to work with Tajikistan to carry forward their traditional friendship, strengthen mutually beneficial cooperation, jointly promote the development and prosperity of the two countries, and better benefit the people of both nations, he said. Li said China looks forward to working with all parties of the SCO to implement the outcomes of the Bishkek summit, ensure the complete success of the upcoming SCO prime ministers' meeting, promote cooperation in various fields to achieve new progress, and bring benefits to the people of all countries in the region. Rasulzoda and other senior government officials greeted Li at the Dushanbe International Airport, and a welcome ceremony was held in his honor. Li traveled to Dushanbe after concluding his official visit to Uzbekistan.

item.title: Chinese vice premier attends world vocational, technical education development conference
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
TIANJIN, Oct. 16 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang attended the 2026 World Vocational and Technical Education Development Conference, which opened in Tianjin on Friday. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said in his speech that vocational education plays an important role in economic and social development. Breakthroughs are accelerating in the new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation, placing higher demands on the training of skilled professionals, Ding said. To boost international vocational education cooperation and development, Ding called for efforts to enhance policy communication and the alignment of rules, and promote the cross-border flow and efficient allocation of skills. He also called for promoting the deep integration of new technologies, such as digital, intelligent and green technologies, with vocational education, and cultivating highly skilled personnel who can better meet the needs of economic and social development. Efforts should also be made to enhance support for less-developed countries and regions, and deepen exchanges and cooperation through skills training and knowledge sharing, Ding said. China now has the world's largest vocational education system, with more than 10 million graduates each year. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), vocational education supplied more than 70 percent of the additional highly skilled workers in the country's modern industries. China has also established 38 Luban Workshops in 32 countries, providing academic education to more than 30,000 students and non-degree training to over 160,000 participants. Previously, the World Vocational and Technical Education Development Conference was held in 2022 and 2024. Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, deputy prime minister of Malaysia, and Khondker M. Talha, president of the 43rd session of the General Conference of UNESCO, addressed the conference in person and via video link, respectively. When meeting with Ahmad Zahid on Thursday in Beijing, Ding said China is ready to work with Malaysia to implement the important consensus reached by leaders of the two countries and advance high-quality cooperation in such areas as infrastructure, high-tech, agriculture and vocational education between the two countries. Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia is committed to further promoting Malaysia-China friendship, better aligning development strategies, and achieving more mutually beneficial and win-win results.

item.title: Xi's decades-long commitment to poverty reduction
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
BEIJING, Oct. 17 -- Poverty eradication is "a common ideal of humanity," Chinese President Xi Jinping has once said. Five years after China declared a complete victory in the fight against absolute poverty in 2021, its approach continues to inspire poverty reduction efforts worldwide. Xi's dedication to poverty alleviation spans decades, from his early work in poor rural communities to the nationwide campaign he led and his efforts to promote international cooperation -- a long-running endeavor that resonates as the world marks the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty on Saturday. A DECADES-LONG PURSUIT "A weak hatchling bird can be the first to fly, and the poorest can be the first to become rich," Xi wrote in a 1988 essay on the development of Ningde Prefecture in east China's Fujian Province. The following summer, Xi, then Ningde's Party secretary, traveled by car and on foot to reach Xiadang, a remote mountain township that had no road access. Xi returned to Xiadang twice, helping tackle problems with roads, electricity and water supplies. In 2019, residents wrote to tell him that their township had shaken off poverty, and he replied with congratulations. After becoming China's top leader, Xi continued his hands-on approach to poverty reduction. He conducted more than 50 inspections and research visits related to poverty alleviation, traveling to all 14 of the country's contiguous areas of extreme poverty. In February 2018, Xi visited impoverished Yi families in Zhaojue County, Sichuan Province, asking about their livelihoods and discussing ways to tackle poverty with villagers and local officials. "Not a single ethnic group or family should be left behind in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects," he said during the visit. On Feb. 25, 2021, Xi declared a "complete victory" in China's fight against absolute poverty. Over eight years, nearly 100 million rural residents had been lifted out of absolute poverty, enabling the country to meet the poverty reduction target of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development a decade ahead of schedule. In a congratulatory letter to Xi, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the achievement "a reason for hope and inspiration to the entire community of nations." LESSONS BEYOND BORDERS China's poverty reduction experience has attracted attention from leaders around the world, some of whom have sought inspiration from Xi's writings and visited places where his ideas were put into practice. Xi's early ideas on poverty reduction and economic development were collected in "Up and Out of Poverty," a collection of speeches, articles and interviews from 1988 to 1990 during his tenure in Ningde. Explaining the title, Xi wrote that its significance lay first and foremost in uprooting the "poverty mentality" and "poverty thinking." In a foreword to the book's Uzbek edition published in 2023, President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev said the work remained an important source of guidance for state and social governance more than three decades after its initial publication. During his visit to China this month, President of Botswana Duma Gideon Boko traveled to Fuzhou and Ningde in Fujian Province, where Xi once worked, and visited an exhibition on poverty reduction. During talks with Xi in Beijing, Boko depicted China's development as "an economic and political miracle never seen in history." In June 2018, Bounnhang Vorachith, then President of Laos, visited Shibadong Village in central China's Hunan Province to learn about China's approach to poverty reduction. In villager Shi Basan's home, he paused before a photograph showing Xi chatting with her beside a fire pit. During that November 2013 visit, Xi first proposed "targeted poverty alleviation" in a discussion with villagers, calling for measures tailored to local conditions and each household's needs. After retracing Xi's route and speaking with residents, Bounnhang voiced hope of bringing the village's experience back to Laos. In reply to a letter from the villagers the following year, he praised Shibadong's success as offering invaluable lessons for his country. In September 2026, Prime Minister of Madagascar Mamitiana Rajaonarison also visited Shibadong, where he witnessed first-hand residents' changing lives and watched demonstrations of traditional Miao ethnic embroidery. He said the visit shown him Xi's deep concern for the people and provided inspiration for Madagascar. TURNING EXPERIENCE INTO ACTION Xi's efforts to share China's poverty reduction experience abroad date back to his early tenure in Fujian Province. There, he promoted Juncao technology as part of Fujian's poverty reduction cooperation with northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. In 2000, he introduced the technology to a visiting governor from Papua New Guinea and later helped establish a China-aided Juncao demonstration base in the Pacific island country. Juncao technology uses grass to cultivate mushrooms and provide livestock feed. The technology has spread to more than 100 countries, creating hundreds of thousands of jobs. In Zimbabwe, farmer Mandiudza Masvongo has earned 330 U.S. dollars from selling mushrooms since taking up Juncao cultivation in June 2025. The proceeds have helped her start a small cleaning products business, which she said could mark a turning point in her life. Beyond agriculture, China's development assistance has also improved basic services and created opportunities for small businesses. In Cambodia's Tanorn village, a China-aided project brought better roads, clean water and solar power. Por Sokhim, once dependent on rice farming, now runs a grocery store, while her husband operates a motorcycle repair shop. In 2021, Xi proposed the Global Development Initiative, with poverty reduction and food security among its priorities. In the five years since its launch, cooperation projects under the initiative have taken root and delivered tangible results in more than 120 countries. At the 2024 G20 summit in Rio de Janeiro, Xi drew upon China's experience to express confidence in the prospects for poverty reduction across the developing world. "If China can make it, other developing countries can make it too. This is what China's battle against poverty says to the world," he told world leaders.

item.title: Xi congratulates Hunan University on its centenary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday extended congratulations to faculty, students and alumni of Hunan University as it marks its 100th anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a congratulatory letter to the university. Xi urged the university to carry forward fine revolutionary traditions, continue to elevate the quality and levels of its teaching, and strive to nurture more talent who can apply their knowledge to practical affairs, so as to make new contributions to building China into an education powerhouse and advancing Chinese modernization. Founded in 1926, Hunan University has nurtured a wealth of outstanding talent over the past century.

item.title: Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development Updated: October 16, 2026 18:55Xinhua ULANQAB, Inner Mongolia, Oct. 16 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded. During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area. He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner. Xi visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry. Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule. He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces. Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes.

item.title: Xi calls for decisive progress in Healthy China advancement
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 13 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to firmly follow a path with Chinese characteristics in developing the country's health programs, to secure decisive progress in the Healthy China Initiative over the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a national meeting on health held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Xi stressed that people's health is a key benchmark of a nation's prosperity and strength. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the Party has made a major decision to launch the Healthy China Initiative, promoting the establishment of the world's largest systems of medical services, traditional medicine, disease prevention and control, and healthcare security, said Xi, noting that the country has achieved historic accomplishments and made all-round progress in healthcare. In 2025, China's average life expectancy rose to 79.25 years, while its major health indicators remained at the leading position among upper-middle-income countries and countries with a population exceeding 100 million. Xi said the goal is to build a Healthy China, where health services are ensured in a balanced, inclusive, high-quality and efficient manner. Xi stressed that people's health should be factored into all policies and reflected in every aspect of work. Prevention, he said, is the most cost-effective and efficient approach to protecting public health. He called for greater emphasis on foundational health work, addressing risks at their source, and encouraging the public to adopt a sound understanding of health and take an active role in managing their own well-being. He also called for a stronger disease prevention and control system to guard against large-scale outbreaks. Xi underscored the need to optimize the functions and structural layout of medical institutions so that people can access medical care close to home and receive effective treatment. China has supported the development of 125 regional medical centers in areas where high-quality medical resources are relatively scarce. Notably, more than 90 percent of residents can access nearby medical and healthcare services within 15 minutes, while primary-level medical institutions account for over 50 percent of all medical visits nationwide. He also urged efforts to improve mechanisms for the preservation and innovative development of traditional Chinese medicine, strengthen basic research and original innovation in the health sector, and enhance the patient experience. Xi stressed that coordinating the development and regulation of medical services, medical insurance, and pharmaceuticals should be a key priority in reforming China's medical and healthcare systems. He also called for efforts to train and develop a sufficient number of highly qualified medical professionals. Efforts will also be made to actively promote the building of a global community of health for all, work with other countries to address major challenges in the health sector, and continuously improve the health and well-being of people around the world, he said. Other Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the event. In his concluding remarks, Li Qiang said Xi's important speech provided guidance for advancing China's health sector. Li called for better coordination between improvements in public health and economic and social development, and urged deeper reform, innovation, opening up and cooperation, stronger prevention and control of major diseases, further development of a tiered diagnosis and treatment system, and greater use of science and technology to improve health services.

item.title: China issues guidelines on developing new quality productive forces
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
BEIJING, Oct. 9 -- The Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council have issued a set of guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces to bolster high-quality development. These guidelines outline 19 key measures in five areas, namely advancing scientific and technological innovation, deepening the integration of sci-tech and industrial innovation, innovating development approaches, promoting institutional and mechanism innovation, and improving mechanisms for talent development. Noting that developing new quality productive forces is an intrinsic requirement and an important focus of promoting high-quality development, these guidelines stress the importance of innovation-driven development, reform and measures tailored to local conditions, and following the approach of "establishing the new before abolishing the old." The guidelines call for pursuing high technology, high efficiency and high quality, properly handling the relationships between the government and the market, between the qualitative nature of productive forces and the forms they take in industry and business, between reform and development, and between self-reliance and opening up, while coordinating development and security. "The new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation has opened up broad prospects for developing new quality productive forces. Seizing this historic opportunity requires moving faster to achieve greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology and raising innovation capacity across the board to maintain strategic initiative," said Wang Shengxiao, a researcher with the Party School of the Communist Party of China Central Committee. The guidelines call for stronger original and transformative sci-tech innovation, with major sci-tech projects to focus on strategic, landmark and leading products, targeting the cutting-edge of global science and technology and serving major areas of economic development, major national needs, and people's health. They stress the need for faster breakthroughs in key core technologies, including efforts to promote the high-quality development of key manufacturing industrial chains and implement industrial innovation projects in priority areas. The guidelines emphasize coordinated efforts to strengthen national strategic sci-tech capabilities, giving full play to national laboratories in organizing major national sci-tech projects and building major innovation platforms. The guidelines also urge optimizing the roles and distribution of national sci-tech research institutions, high-level research universities and leading sci-tech enterprises. The guidelines underline the principal role of enterprises in sci-tech innovation, encouraging technology-based small and medium-sized enterprises to increase research and development investment and supporting capable private enterprises in taking the lead in major national technological breakthrough tasks. To speed up the transformation of sci-tech achievements into real productive forces, the guidelines call for leveraging the advantages of China's vast market to better connect technology with the market and advance the development of new quality productive forces on a larger scale. The guidelines also urge upgrading traditional industries through the application of digital, intelligent and green technologies. The country should seek to advance producer services toward greater specialization and the higher end of the value chain, while improving the quality, diversity and convenience of consumer services, according to the guidelines. For emerging industries, the guidelines emphasize efforts to foster their growth and develop new pillar industries. The guidelines encourage greater cross-industry and cross-regional integration, measures to avoid "involution-style" competition, and support eastern regions to help central, western and northeastern regions develop emerging industries in line with local conditions. The guidelines call for forward-looking planning for future industries and emphasize the need to make full use of existing fiscal policies to support their development and guide social capital to steadily increase investment. The guidelines also urge promoting the deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy, optimizing the layout, construction and operation of national data infrastructure, advancing the digital transformation of the manufacturing sector, and building digital industrial clusters with international competitiveness. The guidelines call for fully implementing the "AI Plus" initiative, using artificial intelligence (AI) to transform traditional industries, accelerating innovation in AI and other digital and intelligent technologies, and promoting the widespread application of AI across industries. Efforts are also needed to establish systems for technology monitoring, early risk warning and emergency response to ensure that AI is safe, reliable and controllable, the guidelines note. These guidelines further propose building a green, low-carbon and circular economic system by strengthening green manufacturing, developing green services, expanding the green energy industry, and driving the supply of green products via green consumption. Efforts should be made to optimize the policy toolbox for green development and implement fiscal, financial, investment, pricing, technological and environmental policies that promote green and low-carbon development, according to the guidelines. The country will actively advance the energy revolution and accelerate the green transition of energy use in production and daily life across society, the guidelines add. The guidelines call for deepening reform to promote close integration of science and technology with the economy, saying that efforts should be made to build an open, shared and secure nationally integrated data market. The guidelines also stress the need to improve the market regulation system and increase the supply of innovative financial products. The guidelines pledge to allocate advanced production factors globally by expanding high-standard opening up and actively building a global innovation cooperation network, and encouraging foreign venture capital institutions, international standards organizations and others to develop in China. The guidelines urge cultivating talent urgently needed for the development of new quality productive forces, adding that policies on the use and flow of talent should be improved. "New quality productive forces are primarily driven by transformational technological breakthroughs, which bring profound changes to how innovation is organized, industries evolve and resources are allocated," said Liu Zhenzhong, a researcher at the Institute of Industrial and Technological Economics of the National Development and Reform Commission. "These changes require deeper reforms to reshape institutional frameworks and remove obstacles to development." The outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) identifies the development of new quality productive forces as a key strategic task and sets out 28 major projects related to this goal, accounting for 25.7 percent of the 109 major projects outlined in the plan. The projects focus on four priorities: strengthening industrial capabilities and competitiveness, fostering emerging industries, pursuing breakthroughs in cutting-edge technologies, and enhancing innovation capabilities. At an international seminar held in Beijing in September, Chinese experts said China's development of new quality productive forces could provide fresh momentum for global economic growth and create new opportunities for countries at different stages of modernization. Abdulrahman Bello Dambazau, Nigeria's ambassador to China, noted that the emphasis on talent development, scientific research and industrial upgrading could offer useful reference for developing countries. China's development of high-tech, green and intelligent industries is also creating more opportunities for cross-border investment and industrial cooperation. At the China International Fair for Investment and Trade in September, representatives from European countries explored cooperation with China in areas such as clean energy, AI, smart manufacturing, biomedicine and the digital economy.
